question: Using the joined Richmond site, separate physical plant sale/closure, the 1996 enforcement respondent, contractual O&M succession and later replacement order. Does plant sale or cessation terminate the inherited cleanup duty?
answer: The 2020 ESD reports the 1996 Lucent-to-Viasystems sale while Lucent remained the 1996 order respondent; manufacturing ceased in June 2001. Viasystems sold the facility to Laburnum Investments on August 23, 2006 for redevelopment. Agere undertook O&M on Lucent’s behalf, and its April 2, 2007 acquisition by LSI continued that role. The 2013 order replaced the 1996 order and named LSI and Alcatel-Lucent as respondents; later parent transactions did not by themselves end that obligation. The Target covenant separately retains Lucent’s historic respondent role and LSI O&M. These are different property, contract and regulatory roles, not a proved private indemnity or present closure finding.

question: Follow the fourth ESD’s permission to transition from pumping to attenuation to its prerequisites, monitoring stages and retained contingency plan. Register the conditions instead of treating final approval as evidence that pumping has already stopped permanently.
answer: After source removal and necessary hotspot treatment, EPA evaluates monitoring data for cleanup goals at all points of compliance. Stable or decreasing concentrations permit the system to remain shut down only with quarterly monitoring for one year (four events), semiannual monitoring for one year (two events), then annual monitoring until all-point cleanup goals are met, plus the contingency plan. The 2015 plan remains until those goals are met; perimeter-well contingency-value exceedance triggers contingent action such as resampling, restart, biological treatment or ISCO. The profile’s operational-improvement history is separate from proof that these later conditions or cleanup endpoints were achieved.

question: After resolving the BRE supplemental and Target parcel instruments, register recording, proof-delivery, transfer notification, conveyance notice and retained access duties. What changes to the earlier covenant does BRE’s supplemental instrument actually authorize?
answer: BRE’s supplement expressly adds to and neither terminates nor amends the earlier covenant recorded May 20, 2013. It grants remedy access and requires future conveyance notice. Both selected instruments distinguish recording within ninety days of agency approval (amendments/assignments/termination within ninety days of execution), stamped-copy delivery within sixty days of recording, and transfer notice to EPA/DEQ within thirty calendar days. BRE’s holder must avoid practicable business interference and repair damage at its cost; Target preserves remedy access too. These duties do not establish that transfers, proof delivery or timely recording occurred merely because a instrument is posted.

question: Compare the older SB and the later fourth ESD with the 2026 EPA profile. What selected-remedy changes are supported, and what apparent profile omissions cannot establish an implemented shutdown or a new 2026 remedy event?
answer: The 1991 SB describes preliminary selection; the fourth ESD reports a January 22, 2020 draft, comment close February 21, 2020 and no comments, so final modifications are unchanged. It adds source-removal/hotspot/conditional attenuation measures plus dioxane and vinyl chloride cleanup goals. The 2026 profile still recounts the original pumping system, the 2015 pilot and older improvement history rather than a complete fourth-ESD implementation chronology. A page update or omitted newer detail is not a new event, proof of absent obligations or proof of permanent shutdown. Preserve the dated version and approved conditions while requesting implementation evidence.

evidence.quote: In September 1996 EPA issued an Administrative Order to Lucent Technologies Inc. requiring groundwater remediation, through a pump and treat system to drinking water standards. That system included 18 groundwater extraction wells; a treatment system with air strippers, carbon adsorption, solvent recovery, chemical feed and iron removal; and environmental sampling of surface water, groundwater and associated reporting. In December of 2015 a pilot test was initiated to evaluate operational changes to the site’s groundwater treatment system and has resulted in operational modifications and efficiencies with regard to achieving cleanup goals. Although EPA issued a Corrective Action Statement of Basis Complete with Controls to AT&T in May 1991, in the Spring of 2000, Lucent implemented a series of improvements to enhance performance of the existing groundwater remediation system. These enhancements included: Installation of four new perimeter extraction wells to cut off flow along an apparent preferential pathway Installation of a new extraction well in the source area Modification of the three existing extraction wells and the new source area extraction well to vacuum-enhanced recovery Rehabilitation of the perimeter extraction wells Revision of the operation and maintenance of the extraction and treatment system to minimize downtime. A review of the groundwater data collected to monitor the performance of the remediation system indicates that overall the facility contaminants of concern have been contained, the levels have been reduced and the groundwater recovery system is operating as intended. In the Fall of 2006 field activities were initiated to prepare the site for redevelopment. Prior to designing the redevelopment plans, EPA, the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (VDEQ), and the property owners (current and past) participated in multiple meetings and discussions with the developer to ensure that the on-site groundwater remediation system remains operational and protective of human health and the environment. The redevelopment project now known as "The Shops at White Oak Village," includes three large anchor tenants, regional and local retail, a hotel, and restaurants. Initial store openings occurred in October 2008. EPA and VDEQ will continue to monitor the performance of the groundwater remediation system until the cleanup objectives have been achieved. question: Draft a scored acquisition finding for this former manufacturing site, using retained respondent/O&M roles, parcel-specific use restrictions and the conditional newer remedy. Which current evidence should be requested without declaring the shopping-center sale a cleanup release?
answer: Separate the historic manufacturing entity, later parcel owners and LSI/Alcatel remedy respondents. A 1996/2006 sale, cessation in 2001 or retail opening does not establish cleanup release. The fourth ESD’s staged shutdown/attenuation is conditioned on data, monitoring and contingency action; parcel controls run with the land. Request current all-point monitoring, contingency implementation, covenants for the exact acquired parcel, any written vapor/earthmoving exception or plume-distance removal and owner/holder access/notification evidence. The prospective site review should identify inherited obligations without inventing current violations, private indemnity, complete restoration or an absent registry value.
